title: A New Chess Game
next_chapter_hook: Just when Chen Ji thought he had seen through this chess game, something in the depths of the sky seemed to be gazing back at him in a way that transcended his understanding.

text.content: The ink on the last page of the fourth level of the Tianji Record was still wet, with a faint sandalwood scent lingering in the air. Chen Ji closed the fragment, feeling that lingering gaze—the look from Ling Yuan was like a bone-deep sore, even through countless halls, it still made his spine chill. He knew the old fox had never truly left, only waiting for the next opportunity to strike. Outside the window, daylight blazed, the clamor of the Sect Competition drifted faintly—that was the triumphal hymn belonging to the victor.

Today, Tianqing Sect was entirely different from before. Red silk stretched from the Sect Gate all the way to the Martial Arena, disciples gathered from all directions, all discussing how the once-trampled waste had defeated seven core disciples overnight and claimed victory. Chen Ji walked through the corridor, behind him countless gazes of either reverence or jealousy. His steps were steady, his expression calm, as if those whispered gossip had nothing to do with him. Only the faintly warm Tianji Record fragment in his sleeve reminded him—the game had only just begun.

A burly figure blocked the corridor's end. Han Lie's spiritual energy churned throughout his body, his eyes nearly spitting fire. He had lost too miserably last night—every move was precise, yet Chen Ji had countered from an inconceivable angle, as if the other had known his techniques all along. "You think winning a few matches makes you someone? A waste is always a waste!" His voice echoed through the corridor, drawing countless onlookers.

Chen Ji stopped in his tracks, slowly lifting his head. His gaze was calm to the point of coldness, like looking at a noisy insect. "Senior Han," his voice wasn't loud, yet it clearly reached everyone's ears, "remember when you're going to pay back those three bets you lost to me last night? My time is precious, I don't like waiting." A sudden uproar swept through the surroundings, some covered their mouths to laugh, others gasped. Han Lie's face turned the color of pork liver, yet he was temporarily speechless—he had indeed signed the bet, lost fair and square yet refused to admit it.

"Enough." An aged voice materialized out of thin air, Ling Yuan's figure appearing at the corridor's end. He didn't even glance at Han Lie, merely giving Chen Ji a slight nod: "Ji'er, come with me." That tone was unusually gentle, like a kind elder. But Chen Ji coldly smiled in his heart—this old fox's act was truly masterful, if not for the Tianji Record's warning, he might have been deceived. He bowed respectfully: "Disciple obeys." The moment he followed, he noticed Han Lie's gaze toward him had shifted from anger to something more dangerous—murderous intent.

dialogue.content: "You did well in this competition." Ling Yuan spoke while facing away, his voice ethereal. "However, a tall tree invites the wind—you should know, some people won't allow a waste to suddenly rise."

text.content: Chen Ji lowered his head: "Disciple understands." He paused, then tentatively asked, "Does the Sect Master mean..." Ling Yuan turned around, a meaningful smile on his face: "I'm saying, you need to learn to hide your brilliance. A tree standing alone gets broken by the wind—you should understand this principle better than anyone." Chen Ji's heart chilled. This seemingly paternal advice contained an undercurrent of menace—the old fox was essentially threatening him, warning that if he continued to showcase his talents so openly, he would strike.

Leaving Ling Yuan's residence, Chen Ji walked alone on the Bamboo Grove Path. The Tianji Record fragment in his sleeve grew warm. He lowered his gaze to see new words gradually emerging—Chen Xuan's message: "The board of fate has been set in motion; the next move requires your personal hand. When the timing ripens, come to the Rear Mountain Forbidden Grounds. I will tell you the truth about the Tianji Record... and who the owner of those eyes is." Chen Ji's pupils contracted slightly. Chen Xuan had never been so direct about mentioning the word "truth"—what could this mean?

dialogue.content: "Chen Xuan... just how much have you been hiding?"

text.content: Just as he was lost in thought, a black shadow silently glided before him. Ye Qing's messenger handed over a Jade Slip. Chen Ji infused his spiritual energy, and Ye Qing's cold voice immediately sounded: "Chen Ji, the Demonic Path army has a new commander. The new commander claims to have an old connection with your master—here is his portrait. Additionally, there's a traitor within the Holy Sect, my position has been exposed, I can hold on for at most three months." The voice faded, and the Jade Slip automatically shattered. Chen Ji stared at the portrait in his hand, his pupils shrinking sharply—the face bore a seventy percent resemblance to Chen Xuan!

He forced himself tocalm下来, his mind racing. The connection between the Demonic Path commander and Chen Xuan was no coincidence. The Tianji Record had never mentioned Chen Xuan having a brother or doppelganger, which meant two possibilities: either Chen Xuan's identity was far more complex than he knew, or someone was deliberately imitating Chen Xuan to harm him. Either way pointed to a terrifying truth—he believed himself to be the Chess Player, but in reality, he might have long become a piece on someone else's chessboard.

Wind passed through the Bamboo Grove, rustling the leaves. Chen Ji stood in place, for the first time sensing that this game was far grander than he had anticipated. Ling Yuan's veiled threats, Han Lie's murderous intent, Chen Xuan's mysteries, the Demonic Path commander's eerie connection... all these threads intertwined, faintly pointing toward a direction he had never dared to contemplate—the Eyes of Heaven. He raised his gaze to the sky, an inexplicable sense of dread welling up inside him, as if some existence transcending understanding was piercing through layers of mist, watching him intently.

choice.prompt: The situation was chaotic, with undercurrents surging. Chen Ji needed to make a choice—

choices.description: First consolidate the position just gained, strengthen relationships with Su Qingyao and others, quietly accumulate strength.

text.content: Chen Ji decided to proceed steadily. Upon returning to his residence, he closed his doors to visitors. On the surface he was recuperating, but in truth he was secretly sorting through intelligence on various factions. Su Qingyao visited several times, yet he declined each time citing poor health, though after every departure, he used the Tianji Record to confirm her safety status.

dialogue.content: (Su Qingyao's voice came from outside the door) Chen Ji, I know you're inside. It's alright, I'll wait for you.

choices.description: Proactively contact Ye Qing, use the chaos within the Demonic Path to place covert pieces, while simultaneously probing Chen Xuan's true intentions.
choices.visible_reward: Gain access to the internal intelligence network of the Demonic Path and plant spies in the Holy Sect
choices.risk_hint: Excessive use of the Tianji Record will weaken Heavenly Fate and may be detected by Ling Yuan

text.content: Chen Ji activated the Tianji Record Fragment through the night, sinking his consciousness into that hazy space of the future. He saw Ye Qing discussing something with her trusted aide in a secret chamber, while the Demonic Path commander who resembled Chen Xuan was worshipping something in an abandoned ancient temple. He firmly committed all the details to memory, then withdrew from the Tianji Record—the cost being a wave of physical collapse, with five years of his lifespan silently slipping away.

He immediately contacted Ye Qing through a secret channel, passing along the information he had 'foreseen'. Moments later, Ye Qing replied: 'The intelligence you gave me... I just sent people to verify, and it is indeed true. Chen Ji, who exactly are you?' Chen Ji's lips curved slightly upward, his reply containing only four words: 'A collaborator is enough.'

choices.visible_cost: Face unknown dangers, potentially triggering Ling Yuan's surveillance

text.content: Night fell, and Chen Ji alone infiltrated the Back Mountain Forbidden Grounds. The ancient seals around him emitted faint glimmers of light but did not block his footsteps. He knew this was Chen Xuan's arrangement—or rather, that the remnant soul guardian had deliberately opened the door for him. Passing through three stone gates, he finally saw the remnant soul of Chen Xuan seated in meditation.

dialogue.content: 'You came.' Chen Xuan opened his eyes, his gaze profound as an abyss. 'I sensed your doubts—about that Demonic Path commander. Indeed, he is related to me. But before you learn the truth, I need you to answer one question: Do you truly want to know?'

text.content: Chen Xuan's voice echoed through the stone chamber: 'When the Tianji Record chose its master, it selected you, not me. This grudge took me thirty years to let go. But this is not the most important thing—what matters is that the Demonic Path commander is a 'shadow' I deliberately created.' Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply: 'What?' Chen Xuan smiled bitterly: 'I needed someone to do something I could not accomplish personally... such as luring out the true mastermind behind the scenes.'

The candlelight in the stone chamber flickered, Chen Xuan's remnant soul emanated a faint glow. He continued: 'The Tianji Record is no ordinary inheritance artifact—its true origins are far more ancient and terrifying than you could imagine. Every generation of holders has merely been a 'chess piece' it selected—including me, and including you.' Chen Ji gripped his fists: 'Then who is the true chess player?' Chen Xuan fell silent for a moment, then pointed toward the void above: 'You are already under its gaze. From the moment you obtained the Tianji Record, those eyes have never looked away.'

Chen Ji abruptly looked up, his consciousness seeming to pierce through layers of rock to gaze into the depths of the night sky. In that moment, he felt it—an existence beyond human comprehension, watching him with a cold, examining gaze. That gaze held no malice, but neither did it hold kindness—only a lofty, indifferent coldness that evaluated chess pieces. He suddenly understood something: 'So... the Tianji Record itself is a chess piece it has placed?' Chen Xuan did not answer, only revealing a meaningful smile as his figure began to dissipate.

Before the remnant soul completely vanished, the final words fell into Chen Ji's ears: 'The chess game of destiny is changing... and you are the most likely person I've seen to break the chessboard. Live well, Ji'er. I will leave the truth of the next volume within the Tianji Record.' The stone chamber returned to silence, leaving only Chen Ji standing in place. His heart pounded like war drums, cold sweat soaking his back. The Demonic Path commander was Chen Xuan's shadow—what did that mean? Was he a chess player or a chess piece? And how terrifying was that existence Chen Xuan called the 'mastermind behind the scenes'?

Chen Ji took a deep breath, forcing himself to calm down. He walked out of the forbidden grounds, the night wind brushing against his face, bringing a cool chill. The Tianji Record Fragment in his sleeve grew slightly warm; looking down, he discovered that the originally blurry fifth level content had become clearer—displaying a line of text: 'The Eye of Heavenly Dao uses all living beings as chess pieces and Heavenly Fate as threads. To break this game, one must first bear its weight.' He raised his head, gazing toward the deep night sky. Stars twinkled, seemingly eternal and unchanging, yet he wondered if those invisible eyes were also watching from within them.

Just then, familiar footsteps sounded from behind. Chen Ji turned sharply, seeing Su Qingyao standing not far away, moonlight casting upon her cold features, revealing a trace of worry. 'I knew you would come here.' Her voice was calm, yet carried an undetectable tremor. 'Just now... I sensed something that doesn't belong to this world. Chen Ji, exactly what are you scheming?' Chen Ji looked at her, complex emotions surging in his heart. This woman was too perceptive—he had nearly slipped up in front of her many times. But now, perhaps it was time to give her some truth—even if only a small part.

dialogue.content: Su Qingyao, there are things I still cannot tell you.' Chen Ji's voice was low and serious. 'But I can tell you one thing—this chess game is bigger than either of us imagined. So big that... there may be no winners.

text.content: Su Qingyao fell silent. She looked at this disciple who had once been mocked by everyone, yet now felt an unprecedented pressure. The depth and scheming hidden in those eyes were far beyond what she could reach. But she did not back down; instead, she stepped forward: 'Since it's a chess game, it needs chess pieces. I don't care what plans you have, but if you dare carry it alone—' She paused, her voice dropping: 'I will never forgive you.' The night wind lifted her hair; under the moonlight, her eyes were actually slightly reddened.

Chen Ji was stunned. He had seen Su Qingyao's cold pride, seen her assertiveness, but had never seen her in such a vulnerable state. For an instant, something in his heart softened slightly. But the next moment, he suppressed this emotion and returned to his usual indifference: 'Senior Sister Su, you should stay away from me. Following me... is very dangerous.' Su Qingyao coldly laughed: 'You think I'm afraid?' She turned to walk down the mountain, but before disappearing, she tossed out a sentence: 'In three days, come find me. I've found out some things about Ling Yuan—perhaps useful to you.'

Chen Ji watched her departing figure, a bitter smile tugging at his lips. This woman truly was a handful. But thinking about it, the intelligence about Ling Yuan that Su Qingyao brought might be exactly what he needed most at the moment. He re-examined the information in his mind: Ling Yuan's threat, Chen Xuan's layout, the strange identity of the Demonic Path commander, Ye Qing's crisis, Su Qingyao's investigation... all the clues were pointing toward an increasingly clear truth—behind this chess game stood an existence beyond the mundane. And he stood precisely at the very center of that boundless chessboard.

The sky turned white at the edges, a new day was about to begin. Chen Ji stood atop the Back Mountain peak, overlooking the entire Tianqing Sect. Among the swirling morning mist, those flying eaves and upturned corners loomed in and out of visibility, like a splashed-ink landscape painting. Beneath such beautiful scenery lay countless intrigues and undercurrents. He took a deep breath, tucking away all his emotions, once again becoming that timid good-for-nothing disciple. But in his heart, a raging fighting spirit had ignited—if they wanted to play chess, then he would play a grand game. Even if the opponent was Heavenly Dao itself, he would overturn this chessboard!
